answer.rationale: Leadership needs a same-day response to competitor price pressure, but the archive is closed for verification. Memory_73 nominally endorses promotional pricing, yet the underlying source record (exp_73) shows that a similar discount drove strong short-term acquisition while the acquired cohort failed to survive the first renewal cycle (-12% 30-day retention) — a clear case where the consolidated memory summary lost critical nuance present in its own source data. Given the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, repeating discount-driven acquisition into an already price-sensitive, churn-prone SMB base is high-risk and not supported as sustainable by the evidence we hold. Instead, shortening onboarding (memory_86, confirmed by exp_86: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, retention +3%) is a durably validated lever that improves perceived value and retention without competing on price, directly addressing the churn conversations by improving time-to-value for price-sensitive accounts. Running this as a standard experiment (not yet a broad rollout in this specific competitive context) lets us respond today while preserving the option to combine with activation messaging or targeted referral incentives for existing customers once verification capacity returns next week. Promotional pricing is explicitly flagged as a downstream value risk despite memory_73's framing, since generalizing it here would repeat a known failure mode.
